mainTopic: Do חייבי כריתות and חייבי מיתות בית דין also get מלקות? The opinions of רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and רבי יצחק, their sources, and רבא's and רבינא's explanations of the dispute.
overview: This עמוד finishes a ברייתא about whether people who deserve כרת or a בית דין death penalty also get מלקות ארבעים. רבי ישמעאל says both groups get lashes. רבי עקיבא says only חייבי כריתות get lashes. רבי יצחק says neither group does. The גמרא finds רבי ישמעאל's source in ״והפלא״, read as lashes for breaking "all" the Torah. It then limits this to a לאו like muzzling an ox. רבי עקיבא's source is ״כדי רשעתו״, which teaches one punishment per sin, while רבי ישמעאל calls death plus lashes one "extended death." To explain why כרת cases still get lashes, רבי אבהו brings a גזירה שוה, and after objections the sugya limits ״כדי רשעתו״ to court punishments. רבא then recasts the whole argument as a case where the sinner was warned about lashes. רבינא starts another explanation that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: both groups are included in lashes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends רבי ישמעאל's opinion: people who deserve כרת and people who deserve a בית דין death penalty are both included in the law of מלקות ארבעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Those liable to כרת and those liable to a court death penalty] are included in the category of forty lashes. This is the statement of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining a ברייתא in the middle. Its first words were on the previous עמוד. Here רבי ישמעאל finishes saying that both חייבי כריתות and חייבי מיתות בית דין can receive מלקות ארבעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל takes the widest view. Having a heavier punishment, whether from Heaven or from בית דין, does not exempt a person from מלקות. The next two opinions will narrow this down step by step.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty lashes, the court punishment for breaking a לא תעשה (in practice 39 are given)
Included in the category of
They are (included)

phrases.english: [they] are included in the category of forty lashes,
phrases.notes: This sentence started on the previous עמוד: "those liable to כרת and those liable to a בית דין death penalty." The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֶשְׁנָן בִּכְלַל מַלְקוֹת אַרְבָּעִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first opinion of a ברייתא that began on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both חייבי כריתות and חייבי מיתות בית דין are included in מלקות ארבעים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: כרת yes, court death penalty no
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says חייבי כריתות do get מלקות, because תשובה can wipe away their heavenly punishment. חייבי מיתות בית דין do not get מלקות, because תשובה does not stop the earthly בית דין from executing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Those liable to כרת are included in forty lashes, because if they repent, the heavenly court forgives them. Those liable to a court death penalty are not included in forty lashes, because even if they repent, the earthly court does not forgive them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a middle opinion. He agrees with רבי ישמעאל about חייבי כריתות, but he disagrees about חייבי מיתות בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is whether the bigger punishment is certain. כרת can be cancelled by תשובה, so it cannot replace the lashes, and בית דין still gives מלקות. A בית דין execution happens no matter what, so the same court does not add lashes on top for the same sin.

keyTerms.meaning: People who deserve כרת, being cut off by Heaven
People who deserve a death penalty carried out by the court
Repentance
The heavenly court
The earthly human court
Forgive or pardon

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying that כרת is a lighter sin. His point is that כרת can be removed by תשובה while a בית דין execution cannot, and that is why lashes still apply to כרת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Those liable to karet are
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording uses the word in square brackets. Both mean "are."

phrases.english: included in the category of forty lashes,
because if they repented,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה מוֹחֲלִין לָהֶן.
phrases.english: the heavenly court absolves them.
Those liable to court-imposed death penalties
are not included in the category of forty lashes,
because even if they repented,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַטָּה מוֹחֲלִין לָהֶן.
phrases.english: the earthly court does not absolve them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees in part with רבי ישמעאל: agrees about כרת, disagrees about מיתות בית דין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חייבי כריתות get מלקות. חייבי מיתות בית דין do not.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: even כרת cases get no lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says חייבי כריתות also do not get מלקות. All the עריות were already included in a general פסוק of כרת. The Torah took out the case of one's sister and mentioned it separately to teach that the punishment is כרת and not lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: Those liable to כרת were already included in the general rule. So why was כרת singled out for his sister? To judge him with כרת and not with lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives the narrowest opinion. Neither חייבי כריתות nor חייבי מיתות בית דין receive מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the rule of something that was in a כלל and was taken out to teach something. ויקרא 18:29 already gives כרת for all the עריות, yet ויקרא 20:17 repeats כרת for a sister. That repeat must be teaching something new: this sin gets כרת only, with no lashes. The same then applies to all חייבי כריתות.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule or category in a פסוק
Was taken out of the general rule to be mentioned on its own
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven
His sister
To judge him, to set his punishment

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: רבי ישמעאל says both groups get lashes. רבי עקיבא says only כרת cases get lashes. רבי יצחק says neither group gets lashes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak says:
Those liable to karet were included in the general rule,
phrases.notes: The general rule is ויקרא 18:29, which gives כרת for all the forbidden relationships together.

phrases.english: so why was karet singled out regarding his sister?
To sentence him with karet and not with lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר: חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת בַּכְּלָל הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than רבי עקיבא, exempting חייבי כריתות from lashes as well.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חייבי כריתות are punished with כרת and not with מלקות.

steps.title: What is רבי ישמעאל's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל holds that even people who deserve a בית דין death penalty also get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks for the source behind רבי ישמעאל's wide opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's view is the most surprising, since he gives lashes even to someone who will be executed. So the גמרא wants to see which פסוק supports it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the first opinion in the ברייתא and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that even חייבי מיתות בית דין receive מלקות.

steps.title: The punishment for not keeping the whole Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two פסוקים. One speaks of anyone who does not keep all the words of the Torah. The next says ה׳ will make his plagues ״והפלא״.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: ״If you will not observe to do all the words of this Torah,″ and it is written: ″And ה׳ will make your plagues wondrous.″
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by bringing two פסוקים next to each other. The first covers every מצוה, and the second gives a punishment called ״והפלא״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק includes every sin, even ones that carry a death penalty. The second פסוק gives a punishment for all of them, but we do not yet know what ״הפלאה״ means. The next step will explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: You will observe or guard
And He will make wondrous or extraordinary
Your blows or plagues

phrases.english: As it is written:
"If you will not observe to perform
all the matters of this Torah,"
phrases.notes: דברים 28:58

phrases.english: and it is written: "And God will make your plagues wondrous."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:59, the very next פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: אִם לֹא תִשְׁמֹר לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כׇּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about רבי ישמעאל's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the pairing of ״אם לא תשמר... כל דברי התורה״ with the punishment ״והפלא״.

steps.title: ״הפלאה״ means lashes, for every sin
steps.stepSummary: The word ״הפלאה″ is unclear. Since the פסוק about מלקות uses ״והפילו״, we learn that ״הפלאה״ means lashes. That punishment is given for not keeping "all" the Torah, which includes sins that carry a death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ″הפלאה″, I do not know what it is. When it says: ″And the judge shall make him lie down and strike him before him,″ you must say this ″הפלאה″ is lashes. And it is written: ″If you will not observe to do all...″
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the unclear word ״הפלאה״ by comparing it to ״והפילו״ in the פסוק about lashes. Then it goes back to the first פסוק to show that lashes apply to every מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words sound alike (הפלא and הפילו), so ״הפלאה״ is taken to mean מלקות. Since this punishment is tied to "all the words of this Torah," no sin is left out, not even one with a בית דין death penalty. That is exactly רבי ישמעאל's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The unusual punishment described as ״והפלא״
And he shall make him lie down, said of lashes
The judge
You must therefore say
And so on, meaning the rest of the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל's source: ״והפלא״ means lashes (from ״והפילו״), and it applies to "all" the Torah, so even sins with a death penalty get lashes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how רבי ישמעאל reaches his wide rule. The word "all" in the פסוק is what includes even sins that carry a death penalty.

phrases.aramaic: הַפְלָאָה זוֹ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַה הִיא.
phrases.english: This hafla'a, I do not know what it is.
When it says:
"And the judge shall cause him to lie down and be beaten before him,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2. Notice that ״והפילו״ sounds like ״והפלא״. That's the link.

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר הַפְלָאָה זוֹ מַלְקוֹת הִיא,
phrases.english: you must say that this hafla'a is lashes,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״אִם לֹא תִשְׁמֹר לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כׇּל וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and it is written: "If you will not observe to perform all, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפְלָאָה זוֹ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the unclear word from the previous step and completes the source for רבי ישמעאל.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's ruling that even חייבי מיתות בית דין receive מלקות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The link between ״והפלא״ (דברים 28:59) and ״והפילו״ (דברים 25:2), together with "all" in דברים 28:58.

steps.title: Then a positive מצוה should also bring lashes
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק covers 'all' the Torah, someone who fails to do a מצות עשה should also get מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, people who fail to keep a positive מצוה should also get lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from Step 6. If lashes are for breaking 'all' the Torah, that should include not doing a מצות עשה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 used the word 'all' to include sins with a death penalty. But 'all' is very wide, so it should also cover positive מצוות. Yet we know a person is not lashed for failing to do a מצות עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reasoning is right)
People who failed to do a positive מצוה
Also

phrases.english: If so,
those liable for a positive מצוה should also get lashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wide scope of 'all the words of the Torah' used in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation that 'all the Torah' includes every sin, even ones with a death penalty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'all' includes death-penalty sins, it should also include failing to do a מצות עשה, but there are no lashes for that.

steps.title: The word 'guard' means only prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ״אם לא תשמר״, and רבי אילעי teaches that the word ״השמר״ always points to a לא תעשה. So only prohibitions are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'if you will not guard.' This follows רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעי, who said: wherever the Torah says 'guard,' 'lest,' or 'do not,' it is only a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק itself limits the rule to prohibitions, because it uses the word ״תשמר״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'all' in the פסוק is only 'all' the things you must 'guard.' Based on רבי אילעי's rule, 'guarding' language always means a לא תעשה. So a מצות עשה is left out, but death-penalty sins, which are prohibitions, are still in.

keyTerms.meaning: Guard / be careful: language that signals a prohibition
Lest: also signals a prohibition
A negative commandment, a prohibition
It is written

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי אילעי's rule is a general tool used across ש״ס to tell when a פסוק is creating a prohibition.

phrases.english: 'If you will not guard' is written,
phrases.notes: דברים 28:58

phrases.english: and this is like what Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ilai,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַי:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ilai:
Wherever it says
'guard,' 'lest,' or 'do not'
it is nothing but a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7 by limiting the פסוק to prohibitions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual limitation: a word in the פסוק narrows the scope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All the Torah' includes positive מצוות too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״תשמר״ limits the rule to לא תעשה only, so no lashes for a מצות עשה.

steps.title: Then a prohibition without action should also bring lashes
steps.stepSummary: If every לא תעשה is included, then a לאו שאין בו מעשה should also bring מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a prohibition that has no action should also bring lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new answer. If every prohibition is included, then even a לאו broken without doing any action should bring lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said every לא תעשה is covered. But we know there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה. So the rule from Step 8 is still too wide.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition broken without doing a physical action

phrases.english: If so,
a prohibition with no action should also bring lashes!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 8 as still too broad.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every לא תעשה is included in the lashes of ״והפלא״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all prohibitions are included, a לאו שאין בו מעשה should get lashes, but it does not.

steps.title: The word 'to do' requires an action
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק says ״לעשות״, so lashes are only for a prohibition broken by doing an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To do' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the next word in the same פסוק: 'to do.' This shows that lashes are only when an action was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads 'if you will not guard to do.' The word ״לעשות״ adds a second limit: it must be a sin done by an action. So a לאו שאין בו מעשה is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: To do: shows that an action is needed

phrases.english: 'To do' is written.
phrases.notes: This word comes right after ״אם לא תשמר״ in the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 with another word from the same פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual limitation: a second word narrows the scope further
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every לא תעשה brings lashes, even with no action.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״לעשות״ limits lashes to prohibitions done with an action.

steps.title: Then a prohibition fixed by a positive מצוה should also bring lashes
steps.stepSummary: A לאו הניתק לעשה is a prohibition with an action, so it should also bring מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A prohibition that can be fixed by a positive מצוה should also bring lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again. A לאו הניתק לעשה is a prohibition and involves action, so by the rules so far it should get lashes, but it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case passes both limits: it is a לא תעשה ('guard') and it is done with an action ('to do'). Yet the הלכה is no lashes, because the Torah gives a positive מצוה to fix it. The words of the פסוק cannot explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition the Torah lets you fix by doing a positive מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with a מצות עשה alone. Here there is a real prohibition that was broken; the Torah just gives a positive מצוה to fix it afterward.

phrases.english: A prohibition that is linked to a positive מצוה should also bring lashes!
phrases.notes: For example, stealing, where the Torah says to return what was stolen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge that passes both limits from Steps 8 and 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that any prohibition with an action brings lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A לאו הניתק לעשה is a prohibition with action, so it should bring lashes, but the הלכה says it does not.

steps.title: Lashes only for sins like muzzling an ox
steps.stepSummary: Lashes are only for a לאו similar to the לאו of חסימה, muzzling an ox, which is not fixed by a positive מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be similar to the prohibition of muzzling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a new tool: lashes are only for sins that are like the לאו of muzzling an ox, which the Torah puts right next to the laws of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לאו of חסימה is written right after the פרשה of מלקות. So the model for lashes is that לאו. Muzzling cannot be fixed by a positive מצוה, so a לאו הניתק לעשה is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to
Muzzling an ox while it threshes

phrases.english: It must be similar to the prohibition of muzzling.
phrases.notes: דברים 25:4. It comes right after the laws of lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by comparing to the לאו of חסימה instead of using a word from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a model case (the פסוק placed next to the laws of lashes)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any prohibition with an action brings lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a לאו like חסימה brings lashes, so a לאו הניתק לעשה is left out.

steps.title: The muzzling comparison answers every question
steps.stepSummary: Now that we use the comparison to חסימה, it answers all the earlier questions too: מצות עשה and a לאו שאין בו מעשה are also not like muzzling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, all the cases can also be explained as needing to be like the prohibition of muzzling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by saying the one comparison to חסימה solves all three questions at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Muzzling is a לא תעשה, it is done with an action, and it cannot be fixed by a positive מצוה. So a מצות עשה, a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and a לאו הניתק לעשה are all left out for the same reason. The word-by-word answers in Steps 8 and 10 are no longer needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this (point)
All of them

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי ישמעאל, lashes come from 'all the Torah' (״והפלא״), but only for a sin like muzzling an ox. It must be a לא תעשה, done with an action, and not fixable by a positive מצוה.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
all of them too can be answered: it must be like the prohibition of muzzling.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the earlier questions too: the positive מצוה and the prohibition with no action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of Step 12 and uses it for the questions of Steps 7 and 9 as well.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One rule, being like the לאו of חסימה, decides which sins get lashes. It leaves out מצות עשה, a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and a לאו הניתק לעשה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source: only one punishment per sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי עקיבא's reason and answers from the words ״כדי רשעתו״: one sin brings only one punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי עקיבא's reason? The Torah says 'according to his wickedness.' For one wrong you can punish him once, but you cannot punish him twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא holds that a person who deserves death is not also given lashes. It answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״כדי רשעתו״ are singular, so they teach that one wicked act brings one punishment. Death is enough, so lashes are not added on top.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to his wickedness' (דברים 25:2), the פסוק about lashes
A wicked act, a sin
You make him liable (for a punishment)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic principle, 'one sin, one punishment.' The rest of this part of the sugya is built on that principle.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva, what is his reason?
"According to his wickedness" —
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2

phrases.english: for one wickedness you make him liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁתֵּי רִשְׁעָיוֹת.
phrases.english: but you do not make him liable for two wickednesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל and asks for רבי עקיבא's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What פסוק is רבי עקיבא's source for not giving lashes to someone who deserves death?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״כדי רשעתו״ teaches one punishment for one sin, not two.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: death and lashes count as one long punishment
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל limits ״כדי רשעתו״ to death plus money or lashes plus money. He says death plus lashes is just one 'extended death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says that rule applies to death and money, or lashes and money. But death and lashes together are one long death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי ישמעאל deals with the פסוק ״כדי רשעתו״, even though he holds that someone who deserves death can also get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל agrees there is no double punishment. He says, though, that two body punishments are not really 'two': the lashes are simply the start of a longer death. Paying money is a different kind of punishment, so money together with death or lashes really is two.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These words apply' only to a certain case
An 'extended death': lashes and death seen as one long punishment
Money, here meaning a payment as punishment

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל does not reject ״כדי רשעתו״. He accepts it and only limits which pairs of punishments count as 'two.'

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael (would say):
These words apply to death and money,
or lashes and money,
but death and lashes —
it is an extended death.
phrases.notes: Picture the lashes as the first part of the execution, so the two together count as one punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the other side reads the same פסוק that רבי עקיבא uses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״כדי רשעתו״ should stop lashes from being added to death, which would go against רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only forbids a body punishment together with money. Death and lashes together are one 'extended death.'

steps.title: Challenge to רבי עקיבא: what about people liable to כרת?
steps.stepSummary: If one sin brings only one punishment, then people liable to כרת should not get lashes either.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא, if so, people liable to כרת should also not get lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי עקיבא using his own rule. כרת is already one punishment, so lashes would be a second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that people liable to כרת do get lashes. But under ״כדי רשעתו״, כרת plus lashes looks like two punishments for one sin, just like death plus lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: People liable to כרת, being 'cut off' by Heaven
If so, if that is the rule

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva, if so,
those liable to כרת too (should not get lashes)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא's own principle from step 14 against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that people liable to כרת get lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כרת is one punishment. Lashes on top of it break the rule of ״כדי רשעתו״.

steps.title: Repentance cannot be the reason, since they have not repented yet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that תשובה could remove the כרת, then rejects this: at the time of the lashes they have not done תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you say, that they might do תשובה? Right now, at least, they have not done it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a possible defense of רבי עקיבא and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could argue that כרת is not certain, because תשובה cancels it, so lashes are the real punishment. But when the court gives the lashes, the person has not repented, so he still deserves כרת, and the double punishment problem remains.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What would you say?', a way of bringing up a possible answer in order to reject it
Repentance
Now, at least, at this moment

phrases.english: What would you say, that if they do תשובה?
phrases.notes: He means: תשובה removes the כרת, so the lashes would end up being the only punishment.

phrases.english: Now, at least, they have not done it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a likely answer to the קשיא of step 16, so the challenge still stands.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested defense that תשובה removes the כרת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: At the moment of the lashes no תשובה has happened yet, so the person is still liable to כרת.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a גזירה שוה openly includes כרת cases in lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the Torah itself includes people liable to כרת in lashes, through the גזירה שוה of ״לעיני״ and ״לעיניך״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The Torah clearly included people liable to כרת in lashes. It learns 'before the eyes of' from 'before your eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the challenge to רבי עקיבא by showing a special Torah source that adds lashes for כרת sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule ״כדי רשעתו״ normally blocks a second punishment. A גזירה שוה can still be an explicit Torah exception. The word ״לעיני״ in the כרת פסוק links to ״לעיניך״ in the lashes פסוק, so כרת sins get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah clearly included
Since it learns, here through a גזירה שוה
'Before the eyes of' / 'before your eyes', the matching words of the גזירה שוה
Lashes

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: בְּפֵירוּשׁ רִיבְּתָה תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said: The Torah clearly included
those liable to כרת for lashes,
since it learns "before the eyes of" from "before your eyes."
phrases.notes: ״לעיני״ is from ויקרא 20:17, a כרת case. ״לעיניך״ is from דברים 25:3, about lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בְּפֵירוּשׁ רִיבְּתָה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 with a new source, now that the תשובה answer in step 17 has been rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special Torah source (גזירה שוה) that makes an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״כדי רשעתו״ should block lashes for people liable to כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גזירה שוה clearly adds lashes for כרת sins, as an exception to the general rule.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר ממל: then court death cases should be included too
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל objects that a similar גזירה שוה (״מעיני״ / ״לעיניך״) should then add lashes for people liable to court-imposed death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל challenged it: If so, people liable to court death should also be included. Let us learn 'from the eyes of' from 'before your eyes'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל attacks רבי אבהו's method: if word links like this work, a similar link should give lashes to people liable to court death too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״מעיני״ appears in a פסוק about עבודה זרה, a sin punished with court death. If ״לעיני״ is enough for a גזירה שוה with ״לעיניך״, then ״מעיני״ should be enough too, and that would go against רבי עקיבא's view that people liable to death do not get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it, raised a strong objection
People liable to a death penalty carried out by the court
'From the eyes of', the matching word in the עבודה זרה פסוק
Let us learn (through a גזירה שוה)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין נָמֵי,
phrases.english: If so, those liable to court death penalties too,
let us learn "from the eyes of" from "before your eyes"!
phrases.notes: ״מעיני״ is from במדבר 15:24, a פסוק about עבודה זרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's גזירה שוה from step 18 by showing it proves too much.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a similar word is enough to link to the lashes פסוק, then ״מעיני″ in a court-death case should link as well. That would give lashes to people liable to death, against רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Only matching word-forms can be compared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבא בר ממל. ״לעיני״ can be compared to ״לעיניך״ because both start with ל. But ״מעיני″ starts with מ, so it cannot be compared.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may learn ״לעיני״ from ״לעיניך״, but we may not learn ״מעיני״ from ״לעיניך״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection from step 19. It says the word ״מעיני״ is not similar enough to ״לעיניך״ to build a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא בר ממל wanted to use ״מעיני״ to add lashes for people liable to death by the court. This reply says a גזירה שוה needs a closer match in wording. ״לעיני״ and ״לעיניך״ both have the ל prefix, but ״מעיני״ has a מ prefix, so the link fails.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or derive (one law from another)
Before the eyes of (word in the כָּרֵת verse)
Before your eyes (word in the lashes verse)
From the eyes of (word linked to court death penalties)

phrases.english: We derive “before the eyes of” from “before your eyes,”
but we do not derive “from the eyes of” from “before your eyes.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the objection of step 19 by pointing to the difference in the word prefix.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אבא בר ממל's proposed גזירה שוה of ״מעיני״ / ״לעיניך״.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words are not similar enough: ל versus מ prefix.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the wording: a גזירה שוה needs matching word-forms
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If ״לעיני״ links to ״לעיניך״, then ״מעיני״ should link too, and חייבי מיתות בית דין would get lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ״לעיני״, with the same ל prefix, links to ״לעיניך״. ״מעיני″ does not, so חייבי מיתות בית דין are not brought into lashes.

steps.title: Even very different words can make a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a small prefix difference should matter. The school of רבי ישמעאל linked ״ושב הכהן״ with ״ובא הכהן״, and those are completely different words.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does that make? The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that ״ושב הכהן״ and ״ובא הכהן״ are the same: returning and coming mean the same thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 20. It brings a case where a גזירה שוה was built from two words that are much less alike than ״מעיני″ and ״לעיניך″.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of צרעת on houses, ״שיבה״ (returning) and ״ביאה״ (coming) are different words, yet they were linked. If that works, a small ל versus מ difference cannot block a גזירה שוה. So the defense in step 20 seems too weak.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
Returning (from ״וְשָׁב הַכֹּהֵן״)
Coming (from ״וּבָא הַכֹּהֵן״)

phrases.english: And what difference does it make?
But didn't the school of Rabbi Yishmael teach:
“And the priest shall return,” “And the priest shall come,”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and ויקרא 14:44, both about checking a house with צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה וְזוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!
phrases.english: this is returning and this is coming!
phrases.notes: He means: these two different words are treated as one for a גזירה שוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי נָפְקָא מִינֵּיהּ? וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 20 that ״מעיני״ cannot be compared to ״לעיניך״ because of the prefix.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה שוה was made from entirely different words (״ושב״ / ״ובא״), so a small prefix difference cannot matter.

steps.title: Link ״מעיני״ to ״לעיני״ instead
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: even without a direct link to ״לעיניך״, ״מעיני״ could be learned from ״לעיני״, which is already linked to ״לעיניך״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: let us learn ״מעיני״ from ״לעיני״, since ״לעיני״ was already learned from ״לעיניך״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack on step 20. It suggests a chain that brings court death penalties into lashes anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״מעיני״ and ״לעיני״ are almost the same word. So ״מעיני״ could be linked to ״לעיני״, and ״לעיני″ is already linked to ״לעיניך″ (lashes). The result is the same problem as step 19: people liable to court death should get lashes too.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introducing a second challenge)
Let us learn or derive

phrases.english: And furthermore:
let us derive “from the eyes of” from “before the eyes of,”
since “before the eyes of” was derived from “before your eyes”!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the defense in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The defense in step 20 that blocks ״מעיני״ from the lashes גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״מעיני״ closely matches ״לעיני״, which already links to ״לעיניך״, so the chain brings court death penalties into lashes after all.

steps.title: ״כדי רשעתו״ only counts court punishments
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק gives a new answer. The rule of one punishment per sin applies only to punishments given to the court. כרת comes from Heaven, so it does not block lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק received this teaching: ״כדי רשעתו״ means you punish him for one wickedness, not for two. The verse is speaking about a wickedness that is given over to the court.
steps.whatsHappening: After the גזירה שוה ran into trouble, the גמרא brings a different answer. It explains why people liable to כרת still get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in step 16 was that ״כדי רשעתו״ seemed to forbid two punishments for one sin. The answer is that the verse only means two punishments carried out by a בית דין. כרת is in Heaven's hands, so lashes plus כרת is allowed. Court death plus lashes is still not allowed, because both are court punishments.

keyTerms.meaning: He received it from him (accepted a teaching)
According to his wickedness (דברים 25:2)
A wicked act, or the punishment due for it
Given over to the court's authority
Spiritual cutting off, a punishment from Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: The lashes-plus-כרת question is answered by limiting ״כדי רשעתו״ to court punishments. כרת is from Heaven, so it does not count as a second punishment, and lashes can still be given.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean lashes can always be added to any punishment. Court death plus lashes is still blocked, because both are punishments of the בית דין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why people liable to כרת can be given lashes. It also explains why people liable to court death do not get lashes, which settles the objection of step 19.

phrases.aramaic: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak received it from him:
phrases.notes: He accepted רבי אבא בר ממל's objection to the גזירה שוה, so he explains רבי עקיבא another way.

phrases.english: “According to his wickedness”:
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2

phrases.english: for one wickedness you make him liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁתֵּי רִשְׁעָיוֹת –
phrases.english: but you do not make him liable for two wickednesses;
about a wickedness that is given over to the court
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the troubled גזירה שוה approach and answers the question of step 16 in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the verse (״כדי רשעתו״ applies only to court punishments).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״כדי רשעתו״ forbids any two punishments for one sin, so כרת should block lashes. To get around that, we needed a גזירה שוה, which turned out to be shaky.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״כדי רשעתו״ only forbids two court punishments. כרת is from Heaven, so lashes can be added. Court death penalties still block lashes.

steps.title: רבא narrows the dispute to a warning about lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that if the sinner was warned about death, everyone agrees he gets only death. The argument is only when he was warned about lashes. רבי ישמעאל says a לאו that warns about court death can bring lashes. רבי עקיבא says it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: If they warned him that he would be killed, everyone agrees he is not both flogged and killed. They argue only when they warned him about lashes. רבי ישמעאל holds that a לאו whose job is to warn about court-imposed death can still bring lashes. רבי עקיבא holds that such a לאו cannot bring lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new way to understand the argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא. He makes it a narrower argument that depends on what the sinner was warned about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody holds that a person gets both lashes and death. The real question is what happens when the warning (התראה) was only for lashes, so death cannot be given. רבי ישמעאל lets the לאו bring lashes in that case. רבי עקיבא says the לאו 'belongs' to the death penalty and cannot bring lashes at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned him before the sin (gave him התראה)
Gets lashes and is also put to death

keyTerms.term: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין
keyTerms.meaning: A Torah prohibition whose job is to serve as the warning for a court-imposed death penalty
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: The 'warning' in אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ is the warning witnesses give the sinner right before he sins. The 'warning' in לְאַזְהָרַת is the Torah's own prohibition. These are two different kinds of warning.

phrases.english: Rava says:
If they warned him that he would be killed,
everyone agrees
that he is not both flogged and put to death.
Where they disagree is when they warned him about lashes.
Rabbi Yishmael holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִין –
phrases.english: a prohibition given as the warning for court-imposed death,
one is flogged for it.
And Rabbi Akiva holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: a prohibition given as the warning for court-imposed death,
one is not flogged for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק's answer, רבא offers a different explanation of the רבי ישמעאל / רבי עקיבא dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought they argue whether a person can get both lashes and death.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees he never gets both. They argue only when the warning was for lashes, about whether a לאו tied to court death can bring lashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees there is never both lashes and death. With a warning about lashes, רבי ישמעאל gives lashes for a לאו tied to court death, and רבי עקיבא does not.

steps.title: Then חייבי כריתות should not be flogged either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: the לאו of חייבי כריתות also looks like it is only there to warn about כרת. So by his logic they should not get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא, if so, those liable to כרת should also not get lashes. Their לאו is also a prohibition given as the warning for כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי עקיבא's rule as רבא explained it. It points out that the same reasoning would also take away lashes from people who are liable to כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a לאו that 'belongs' to a death penalty cannot bring lashes, then a לאו that 'belongs' to כרת should not bring lashes either. Yet חייבי כריתות are known to get lashes. So רבי עקיבא's rule seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: People liable to כרת, a punishment from Heaven
If so (if your reasoning is right)
The Torah's warning for a sin punished with כרת

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva, if so,
those liable to karet too should not be flogged,
since it is a prohibition given as the warning for karet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's position as רבא explained it in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's rule that a לאו given as a warning for a punishment cannot bring lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic should apply to כרת, which would cancel lashes for חייבי כריתות. That goes against the accepted ruling that they are flogged.

steps.title: כרת needs no Torah warning, so the לאו is for lashes
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבא, רב מרדכי says that כרת does not need a Torah warning. We see this from פסח and מילה, which carry כרת with no לאו. So a לאו written by a כרת sin must be there for lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: This is what אבימי from הגרוניא said in רבא's name. Those liable to כרת do not need a warning, because the Torah punished פסח and מילה with כרת even though it never warned against skipping them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that כרת never needs a לאו, so the לאו by כרת sins is free to teach lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who skips the קרבן פסח or מילה gets כרת, yet the Torah has no לאו for these. This proves the Torah can give כרת without any לאו. So when the Torah does write a לאו by a כרת sin, that לאו is not needed for the כרת. It is there to bring lashes, which keeps רבי עקיבא's rule intact.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a Torah warning (a לאו) that comes before the punishment
The קרבן פסח and circumcision, two positive מצוות that carry כרת
The Torah stated a punishment
The Torah gave a warning (wrote a prohibition)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi:
This is what Avimi from Hagronya said
in the name of Rava:
Those liable to karet do not require a warning,
phrases.notes: He means the Torah doesn't need to write a לאו before it gives כרת. This isn't about witnesses warning the sinner.

phrases.english: for with the Paschal offering and circumcision, the Torah gave a punishment
even though it did not give a warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הָכִי אָמַר אֲבִימִי מֵהַגְרוֹנְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the לאו is not needed for the stated punishment, so it is free for lashes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לאו by כרת sins is the warning for כרת, so it should not bring lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: כרת needs no לאו, as פסח and מילה prove. So the לאו by כרת sins teaches lashes.

steps.title: Maybe the לאו is needed for a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the לאו by כרת sins could be needed for a different purpose: to make someone who sins by accident bring a קרבן. After all, no קרבן is brought for פסח and מילה, which have no לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the warning is needed for a קרבן. After all, for פסח and מילה, which have no warning, one does not bring a קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. It offers another job for the לאו by כרת sins, which would mean it is not free to teach lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe a לאו is needed before an accidental sinner brings a קרבן חטאת. That would explain why פסח and מילה, which have no לאו, carry no קרבן. If so, the לאו by כרת sins is busy teaching the קרבן, and we lose the proof that it teaches lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Here: the חטאת offering brought by someone who sinned by accident
He does not bring

phrases.english: But perhaps the warning is for an offering.
For with the Paschal offering and circumcision,
which have no warning,
one does not bring an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the לאו by כרת sins must be for lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לאו could be needed for a קרבן instead. פסח and מילה seem to show this: they have no לאו and also no קרבן.

steps.title: No קרבן for פסח and מילה because they are positive commands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that idea. פסח and מילה carry no קרבן because the whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה for קרבנות. Just as עבודה זרה is a 'sit and do not do' sin, only 'sit and do not do' sins bring a קרבן. That leaves out positive commands like פסח and מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, that is not the reason. Rather, it is because the whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה. Just as עבודה זרה is 'sit and do not do', so too everything that brings a קרבן must be 'sit and do not do'. This leaves out these מצוות, which are 'get up and do'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge. It gives a different reason why פסח and מילה carry no קרבן, so the proof for lashes stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The missing קרבן for פסח and מילה is not because they lack a לאו. It is because a קרבן חטאת applies only to sins done by acting, like עבודה זרה. A person 'breaks' פסח and מילה by doing nothing. So the לאו is not needed for the קרבן, and it remains free to teach lashes for חייבי כריתות.

keyTerms.meaning: Was compared (by a היקש, a comparison the Torah makes)
Idol worship
'Sit and do not do': a prohibition you break by doing an action
'Get up and do': a positive command you break by doing nothing
To exclude

steps.whatToRemember: חייבי כריתות get lashes even according to רבי עקיבא. כרת needs no לאו (פסח and מילה prove it), so the לאו is there for lashes. פסח and מילה carry no קרבן only because they are 'קום עשה‎' מצוות. They do not show that a קרבן depends on a לאו.

phrases.english: There, that is not the reason,
rather, it is because
the entire Torah is compared to idol worship:

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה – שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: just as idol worship is 'sit and do not do',
so too everything that brings an offering is 'sit and do not do',
to exclude these, which are 'get up and do'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge in step 27 and so defends the answer in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a different reason for the case used as proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פסח and מילה have no קרבן because they have no לאו, so a קרבן depends on a לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: They have no קרבן because only 'sit and do not do' sins, like עבודה זרה, bring a קרבן. So the לאו is free to teach lashes.

steps.title: רבינא opens a different answer
steps.stepSummary: רבינא begins his own explanation of why רבי עקיבא gives מלקות to חייבי כריתות. He opens with the word לעולם ("actually").
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא says: Actually...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new answer from רבינא. Only his opening words appear here, and his actual explanation continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לעולם tells us a sage is about to keep an idea the discussion was ready to drop, then explain why it still works. Here רבינא is getting ready to answer the earlier question about רבי עקיבא in a different way than רבא did. Wait for the next lines to see exactly which idea he keeps.

keyTerms.meaning: "Actually" or "really": a signal that the speaker is keeping an earlier idea and will now explain it.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking you have רבינא's answer. לעולם is only the doorway, and his real point comes right after.

phrases.english: Ravina says: Actually,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over רבא's answer (Steps 26–28), רבינא starts a separate answer to the same question about רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation (only its opening appears here)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the only way to explain רבי עקיבא is רבא's reasoning, that כרת needs no warning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated. רבינא's full answer follows in the next lines.
